source_read: Saved PubMed Central page text (PMC2911490, author manuscript), read in full: abstract, Introduction, Method, Results, Tables 1–5 (as text), Discussion and acknowledgments; Figures 1–3 are images (legends only).

anchors.locator: Table 5; Results › Global Cognitive Functioning, 2nd–3rd paragraphs
anchors.note: Anchor text revised after the round-1 snapshot; verdict given on the current text. All values are in Table 5: global 41.26 to 47.94 (impaired abstainers, n=6) and 43.70 to 47.01 (impaired controls, n=6); three-way p=0.061; time × baseline impairment p=0.006; processing speed 45.86 to 54.08 vs 47.50 to 46.08 (p=0.014); motor 44.33 to 54.00 vs 47.08 to 47.00 (p=0.051). 'Gained more in every group' is a reading of Table 5, recomputed: impaired vs unimpaired change 6.7 vs 1.9 (abstainers), 2.0 vs 1.3 (Non-Abstinent), 3.3 vs 2.5 T (controls).

Factual basis confirmed: grouping by reported use over the interval (Method › Participants, 1st paragraph; the Discussion's last paragraph names the lack of biological evidence); only the 121 people with both visits are described, with no baseline attrition. From Table 4 (50.1, SD 3.6, n=25 vs 52.8, SD 5.1, n=38) a Student t-test gives t=2.30, df 61, p=0.025 (Welch p=0.017), recomputed; Table 4's footnote names independent-samples t-tests, and its group column, like Results › Global Cognitive Functioning, 1st paragraph (p>0.05), shows only the Non-Abstinent group differing from controls.

p=0.126 is the three-group group × time interaction (printed F(2,188)=2.11; the error df should be 118), against a time effect F(1,118)=55.12; no pairwise abstainer-versus-control change test is reported. Mean interval 13 months (SD 5.6, range 6–42); global change +3.0 (abstainers) vs +2.7 T (controls), Tables 3–4.
